mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.25% signals accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate financing costs decline.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.25% (p-value > 0.05 in t-test vs. baseline).

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate exceeding 10.0% indicates severe labor market deterioration that reduces consumer spending power and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 45% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 10.0% (p-value > 0.05 in t-test vs. baseline).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) below 600 and retail sales (RSAFS) below 350,000 indicate broad consumer demand contraction that depresses corporate revenue expectations, driving negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of HOUST below 600 and RSAFS below 350,000 does not produce negative 20-day returns in at least 60% of cases (p-value > 0.05 in t-test).

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production (INDPRO below 100) combined with high unemployment (UNRATE above 5.0%) signals a supply-driven economic slowdown that reduces corporate output and profit margins, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: In periods where INDPRO < 100 and UNRATE > 5.0%, the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of cases (p-value > 0.05 in t-test vs. baseline).

mechanism_narrative: Higher housing starts (HOUST) levels indicate strengthening residential sector activity that boosts consumer confidence and corporate revenue growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC between HOUST and 5-day SPX returns is less than 0.03 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Federal funds rate exceeding 0.5% signals active monetary tightening that increases corporate borrowing costs and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 0.5% (p-value > 0.05 in t-test vs. baseline).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous federal funds rate above 0.5% and CPI index above 220 indicate aggressive monetary tightening amid persistent inflation, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days due to compressed earnings multiples.
failure_condition: The joint signal of FEDFUNDS > 0.5% and CPIAUCSL > 220 does not produce negative 20-day returns in at least 60% of cases (p-value > 0.05 in t-test).

mechanism_narrative: High unemployment (UNRATE above 6.0%) combined with low employment levels (PAYEMS below 131,000) indicates severe labor market weakness that suppresses consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: In periods where UNRATE > 6.0% and PAYEMS < 131000, the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of cases (p-value > 0.05 in t-test vs. baseline).
